facts.statement: The genus Bdellodus is monotypic, meaning it contains only one species, B. bollensis.
facts.quote: It is monotypic, containing only the species B. bollensis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Bdellodus have been found in the Toarcian stage of Germany.
facts.quote: It is known from the Toarcian of Germany.

facts.statement: The genus was originally described based on associated teeth.
facts.quote: It was named on an associated dentition.

facts.statement: Bdellodus is often classified within the subfamily Acrodontinae, a group of durophagous (shell-crushing) hybodont sharks.
facts.quote: It is often placed in the subfamily Acrodontinae alongside other durophagous hybodontids.

facts.statement: Bdellodus lived during the Early Jurassic epoch.
facts.quote: Bdellodus is an extinct genus of hybodont from the Early Jurassic epoch of the Jurassic Period.

facts.statement: The time range for Bdellodus is estimated to be between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 174.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus was named by Friedrich August von Quenstedt in 1882 because the teeth appeared coal-black, resembling leech teeth.
rejected.quote: Friedrich August von Quenstedt named them this due to their "coal-black" color which he associated with leeches.
